newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes barely changed.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes barely changed.

text.p: Gold prices were under light pressure from early fund selling on Tuesday afternoon but by the 1400 GMT fixing were holding just above earlier levels.
But dealers and analysts said there was only the possibility of spasmodic recoveries to lighten gold's encircling gloom.
"It doesn't matter if you look on the daily, weekly or monthly chart, they all look evil for gold," said independent technical analyst Elli Gifford.
Gold fixed at $333.70 per ounce against $333.60 this morning, which had represented a fresh 4-1/4 month low for bullion.
Dealers said a slightly easier Comex market reflected renewed fund selling on the exchange. The August futures contract was down $0.40 at $334.90 on the fixing.

The dollar reversed earlier firmness but held support in Europe after the National Association of Purchasing Management (NAPM) index of manufacturing activity fell to 55.7 in June from May's 57.1. The June index was forecast at 56.4.
The Dow rose about 24 points to 7697 on the data.
Dealers said there was some restraint in the markets while the monetary policy advisory Federal Open market Committee (FOMC) held a two-day meeting due to conclude on Wednesday.
The possibility of a rise in U.S. interest rates being suggested by the FOMC has largely been discounted in the gold price, dealers said.
The gold charts have deteriorated in the past few days.

"The chart is dominated by a seven-month downtrend which comes through today at $341.00," said Karen Jones of Credit Suisse First Boston. Any rally would encounter dense resistance approaching the downtrend line.
Also notable for the gold price was the apparent turnaround in the cycle. "In cyclical terms it should be bullish but the cycle has gone into reverse," said Gifford.
She forecast a downside for gold stretching through the $325.00 March 1993 low to $300.00, with $285 "highly" possible. "And it is not even oversold," she said.
Silver was unchanged at $4.66/$4.68 and was recognising some support but still prone to a break to $4.50 and $4.30 if the nearby prop at $4.60 failed, Gifford said.
Platinum and palladium were both firmer as dealers awaited
